title: Removal of exceptional-fibre relations modulo finite jets
statement:
Let $(T,\mathfrak M,k)$ be a nonzero commutative regular local ring, with residue field $k=T/\mathfrak M$ [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-weil-residue-field]. Fix a regular system of parameters $(x_0,\ldots,x_r,y_1,\ldots,y_s)$, where $r,s\geq0$, and put $P=(x_0,\ldots,x_r)$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. Let $\mathfrak a\subseteq P$ be an ideal, put $R=T/\mathfrak a$, $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak M/\mathfrak a$, $I=P/\mathfrak a$, $A=T/P=R/I$, and assume $G=\operatorname{gr}_I R$ is flat over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring, def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Set $S=G\otimes_A k$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] and $B=k[X_0,\ldots,X_r]$, with all variables of degree one [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-pc-standard-graded-algebra].
Assume $R$ is reduced (it has no nonzero nilpotent elements) and no minimal prime of $R$ contains $I$, where a minimal prime contains no strictly smaller prime. Let $z\in\operatorname{Bl}_I(\operatorname{Spec}R)$ be over $\mathfrak m$ and belong to the chart $\operatorname{Spec}R[I/\bar x_0]$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-nagata-affine-blowup, def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring]. Put
$$D_T=T[t_1,\ldots,t_r]/(x_0t_i-x_i:1\leq i\leq r),\qquad T'=(D_T)_{\mathfrak p'},$$ [def-trf-permissible-coordinate-chart-ring]
where $\mathfrak p'$ is the inverse image of $z$ under the surjection $D_T\twoheadrightarrow R[I/\bar x_0]$, $t_i\mapsto\bar x_i/\bar x_0$. Assume $T'$ is regular local, let $R_z=\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Bl}_I(\operatorname{Spec}R),z}$, and put $\mathfrak a'=\ker(T'\twoheadrightarrow R_z)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime].
Let $\mathfrak M'$ be the maximal ideal of $T'$, let $H=(x_0,y_1,\ldots,y_s)T'$, and let $\mathfrak p\subset k[t_1,\ldots,t_r]$ be the prime obtained from $\mathfrak p'$ modulo $\mathfrak M D_T$. Put $L=k[t]_{\mathfrak p}$ and $N=\mathfrak pL$. The quotient $T'/H$ is identified with $L$ via the displayed chart presentation. For a local ring with maximal ideal $K$, define the order of $h$ to be $\sup\{n:h\in K^n\}$ and its finite-order initial form to be $h\bmod K^{n+1}\in K^n/K^{n+1}$ [def-sfb-nodal-tangent-comparison-data].
Let $m\geq1$ and let $f_1,\ldots,f_m\in\mathfrak a$ have finite orders $1\leq d_1\leq\cdots\leq d_m$ and belong to $P^{d_i}$. Suppose their initial forms $\phi_i\in k[X]_{d_i}$ minimally generate $\ker(\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak M}T\to\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak m}R)$ in $\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak M}T=k[X,Y]$ [def-trf-adic-initial-ideal-generator-degrees]. Put $g_i=f_i/x_0^{d_i}\in T'$ using the ambient chart embedding into $T[1/x_0]$. Fix $0\leq b<m$ and an integer $d\geq1$ with $d_j\leq d$ for $j\leq b$ and $d_i\geq d$ for $i>b$. For each $j\leq b$ suppose
$$\phi_j(1,t)/1\in N^{d_j},\qquad q_j=g_j-w_j,\qquad w_j\in H(g_1,\ldots,g_{j-1})T',\qquad\operatorname{ord}_{\mathfrak M'}q_j=d_j.$$
Put $J=(q_1,\ldots,q_b)T'$ and assume the finite-jet generation condition $\mathfrak a'\subseteq J+\mathfrak M'^{\,d}$. Then
$$J\cap(H+\mathfrak M'^{\,d})\subseteq HJ+\mathfrak M'^{\,d}.$$
All intersections and sums here are of ideals of $T'$. The ideal generated by an empty family is zero.

source.place: Hironaka (1970), proof of Lemma 20, (20.3)–(20.12), pp.177–181, isolated as the ideal-intersection assertion used there; the finite-jet generation hypothesis is exactly the use of (iv) in (20.7). Read online at https://scispace.com/pdf/certain-numerical-characters-of-singularities-18d51ii5bz.pdf; archival copy WANTED. ILO VIII 2.3.13 is ancestor motivation only; no Stacks tag states this assertion.

proof.text: Write $\theta_i=\phi_i(1,t)/1$. If $v\in P^h$, expand $v=\sum_{|\alpha|=h}a_\alpha x^\alpha$; then $v/x_0^h=\sum a_\alpha t^{(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_r)}$ lies in the given ambient chart, and modulo $H$ it is the dehomogenization of the degree-$h$ initial class (zero if $v\in\mathfrak M^{h+1}$). In particular $g_i\bmod H=\theta_i$. The chart-ring definition [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring] realizes the target chart inside $R[1/\bar x_0]$, so multiplication by $\bar x_0$ is injective there and after localization. Thus $v\in\mathfrak a\cap P^h$ implies $v/x_0^h\in\mathfrak a'$. Every $g_i$ lies in $\mathfrak a'$. Inducting on the triangular identities $q_j=g_j-w_j$, with $w_j\in H(g_1,\ldots,g_{j-1})$, gives $(q_1,\ldots,q_j)=(g_1,\ldots,g_j)$ for $j\leq b$. Consequently $J\subseteq\mathfrak a'$, $w_j\in HJ$, and $q_j\bmod H=\theta_j$. Also $\mathfrak M'/H=N$, so every member of $N^v$ has a lift in $\mathfrak M'^v$.

source.place: Hironaka, Certain numerical characters of singularities, J. Math. Kyoto Univ. 10 (1970), (19.1)–(19.2), p.176, and the beginning of the proof of Lemma 20, p.177; read online at https://scispace.com/pdf/certain-numerical-characters-of-singularities-18d51ii5bz.pdf. Archival original WANTED; the local ILO PDF is ancestor motivation (VIII 2.3.13), not the text of this lemma. No Stacks tag states this result.

proof.text:
We record the effect of a homogeneous syzygy $\sum_{j\leq b}C_j\phi_j=0$ of total degree $h$, putting $C_j=0$ if $d_j>h$. Lift its coefficients to homogeneous expressions $c_j\in P^{h-d_j}$ in the $x_i$, and put $u=\sum c_jf_j$. Then $u\in\mathfrak a\cap P^h$ and its degree-$h$ initial class is zero, so $u\in\mathfrak M^{h+1}$. By [lem-trf-normal-flat-initial-coefficient-lifting] there are $p_i\in\mathfrak M P^{h-d_i}$, for $d_i\leq h$, with $u-\sum p_if_i=v\in\mathfrak a\cap P^{h+1}$. Divide by $x_0^h$. Expanding $p_i$ into degree-$(h-d_i)$ monomials with coefficients in $\mathfrak M$ shows $p_i/x_0^{h-d_i}\in\mathfrak M T'=H$, since $x_i=x_0t_i$. Step 1 gives $v/x_0^{h+1}\in\mathfrak a'$. Hence
$$u/x_0^h=\sum_{d_i\leq h}(p_i/x_0^{h-d_i})g_i+x_0(v/x_0^{h+1})\in H\mathfrak a'.$$

source.place: Hironaka, Certain numerical characters of singularities, J. Math. Kyoto Univ. 10 (1970), (20.4)–(20.7), pp.178–179; read online at https://scispace.com/pdf/certain-numerical-characters-of-singularities-18d51ii5bz.pdf. Archival original WANTED; the local ILO PDF is ancestor motivation (VIII 2.3.13), not the text of this lemma. No Stacks tag states this result.

proof.text: Take $z\in J\cap(H+\mathfrak M'^d)$ and write $z=\sum_{j\leq b}h_jq_j$. Let $\beta_j=h_j\bmod H$. We construct coefficient replacements, preserving $\sum h_jq_j$ modulo $HJ+\mathfrak M'^d$, until $\beta_j\in N^{\max(d-d_j,0)}$. Initially $\beta_j\in N^{\max(1-d_j,0)}=L$. Suppose at the stage $1\leq e<d$ that $\beta_j\in N^{\max(e-d_j,0)}$ and the current sum still lies in $H+\mathfrak M'^d$. Its image $\sum\beta_j\theta_j$ is in $N^d$. Terms with $d_j>e$ already lie in $N^{e+1}$, since $\theta_j\in N^{d_j}$. Apply [lem-trf-projective-order-leading-syzygies] to the active indices $d_j\leq e$. It gives $h_v\leq e$, homogeneous syzygies $(C_{vj})$, zero on the inactive indices, and $a_v\in N^{e-h_v}$, such that $\beta_j-\sum_v a_v\delta(C_{vj})\in N^{e-d_j+1}$ on the active indices.

source.place: Hironaka, Certain numerical characters of singularities, J. Math. Kyoto Univ. 10 (1970), (20.3)–(20.4), pp.177–178, using Lemma 17, pp.172–173; read online at https://scispace.com/pdf/certain-numerical-characters-of-singularities-18d51ii5bz.pdf. Archival original WANTED; the local ILO PDF is ancestor motivation (VIII 2.3.13), not the text of this lemma. No Stacks tag states this result.

proof.text:
For each of these syzygies choose lifts $c_{vj}$ as in Step 2 and any lifts $A_v\in T'$ of $a_v$. Put $k_j=\sum_v A_vc_{vj}/x_0^{h_v-d_j}$, omitting zero terms with $h_v<d_j$. Step 1 makes all these fractions elements of $T'$, with residue $\delta(C_{vj})$. By Step 2, $\sum_j(c_{vj}/x_0^{h_v-d_j})g_j\in H\mathfrak a'$. Replacing $g_j$ by $q_j$ changes this sum by a member of $HJ$, since every $w_j\in HJ$. Therefore $\sum_j k_jq_j\in H\mathfrak a'$. The assumed finite-jet condition gives
$$H\mathfrak a'\subseteq HJ+H\mathfrak M'^d\subseteq HJ+\mathfrak M'^{d+1}.$$
Replace $h_j$ by $h_j-k_j$. The represented sum changes by a member of $HJ+\mathfrak M'^d$ and remains in $H+\mathfrak M'^d$. Step 3's congruences raise every active residue to $N^{e-d_j+1}$; inactive indices are unchanged and already meet the requirement for stage $e+1$. This proves the induction step with precisely the stated invariant.

source.place: Hironaka, Certain numerical characters of singularities, J. Math. Kyoto Univ. 10 (1970), (20.5)–(20.12), pp.179–181; finite-coefficient version of the same elimination; read online at https://scispace.com/pdf/certain-numerical-characters-of-singularities-18d51ii5bz.pdf. Archival original WANTED; the local ILO PDF is ancestor motivation (VIII 2.3.13), not the text of this lemma. No Stacks tag states this result.

proof.text: After the finitely many stages $e=1,\ldots,d-1$, we have coefficients $h_j$ whose residues are in $N^{\max(d-d_j,0)}$, and whose sum differs from the original $z$ by a member of $HJ+\mathfrak M'^d$. Choose lifts $h_j^0\in\mathfrak M'^{\max(d-d_j,0)}$ of these residues. Then $h_j-h_j^0\in H$ and $h_j^0q_j\in\mathfrak M'^d$, because $q_j$ has order $d_j$. Thus the current sum is in $HJ+\mathfrak M'^d$, and so is $z$. This proves the inclusion. For $b=0$ one has $J=0$. For $d=1$ the induction has no stages and all $q_j$ already lie in $\mathfrak M'$, so the same final argument applies.

source.place: Hironaka, Certain numerical characters of singularities, J. Math. Kyoto Univ. 10 (1970), conclusion of (20.3), p.181; explicit termination of the finite order-raising procedure; read online at https://scispace.com/pdf/certain-numerical-characters-of-singularities-18d51ii5bz.pdf. Archival original WANTED; the local ILO PDF is ancestor motivation (VIII 2.3.13), not the text of this lemma. No Stacks tag states this result.

Step 2: the lifted homogeneous syzygy gives u in a∩P^h∩M^{h+1}, which meets the coefficient-lifting node's hypotheses verbatim. Since MT'=H, u/x0^h lies in H a'. Step 3: on the active indices (d_j≤e) the leading-syzygies node's hypotheses hold (φ_j nonzero, φ_j in U_{d_j}, β_j in N^{e−d_j}, active sum in N^{e+1}). Step 4: the finite-jet hypothesis gives H a' ⊆ HJ+M'^{d+1}, and the induction invariant is correctly carried to e+1. Step 5: lifts in M'^{d−d_j} give the conclusion; the cases b=0 and d=1 are covered. The coefficient-lifting node is true: it follows from lem-trf-normal-flat-double-initial-ideal together with Tor-vanishing from flatness and graded Nakayama, and M^{n+1}∩P^n=MP^n. The leading-syzygies node holds in every case I tested: a rational point, a linear non-maximal prime, the real point (t²+1) where the statement is vacuous, and the inseparable F_p(a) points. ρ:U→gr_N L is injective because a polynomial's degree is at least its multiplicity; beyond the cases where U=k[U_1], the general case rests on Hironaka Lemma 17. statement_change.old_statement:
Let $(T,\mathfrak M,k)$ be a nonzero commutative regular local ring, with residue field $k=T/\mathfrak M$ [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-weil-residue-field]. Fix a regular system of parameters $(x_0,\ldots,x_r,y_1,\ldots,y_s)$, where $r,s\geq0$, and put $P=(x_0,\ldots,x_r)$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. Let $\mathfrak a\subseteq P$ be an ideal, put $R=T/\mathfrak a$, $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak M/\mathfrak a$, $I=P/\mathfrak a$, $A=T/P=R/I$, and assume $G=\operatorname{gr}_I R$ is flat over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring, def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Set $S=G\otimes_A k$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] and $B=k[X_0,\ldots,X_r]$, with all variables of degree one [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-pc-standard-graded-algebra].
Assume $R$ is reduced (it has no nonzero nilpotent elements) and no minimal prime of $R$ contains $I$, where a minimal prime contains no strictly smaller prime. Let $z\in\operatorname{Bl}_I(\operatorname{Spec}R)$ be over $\mathfrak m$ and belong to the chart $\operatorname{Spec}R[I/\bar x_0]$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-nagata-affine-blowup, def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring]. Put
$$D_T=T[t_1,\ldots,t_r]/(x_0t_i-x_i:1\leq i\leq r),\qquad T'=(D_T)_{\mathfrak p'},$$
where $\mathfrak p'$ is the inverse image of $z$ under the surjection $D_T\twoheadrightarrow R[I/\bar x_0]$, $t_i\mapsto\bar x_i/\bar x_0$. Assume $T'$ is regular local, let $R_z=\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Bl}_I(\operatorname{Spec}R),z}$, and put $\mathfrak a'=\ker(T'\twoheadrightarrow R_z)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime].
Let $\mathfrak M'$ be the maximal ideal of $T'$, let $H=(x_0,y_1,\ldots,y_s)T'$, and let $\mathfrak p\subset k[t_1,\ldots,t_r]$ be the prime obtained from $\mathfrak p'$ modulo $\mathfrak M D_T$. Put $L=k[t]_{\mathfrak p}$ and $N=\mathfrak pL$. The quotient $T'/H$ is identified with $L$ via the displayed chart presentation. For a local ring with maximal ideal $K$, define the order of $h$ to be $\sup\{n:h\in K^n\}$ and its finite-order initial form to be $h\bmod K^{n+1}\in K^n/K^{n+1}$.
Let $m\geq1$ and let $f_1,\ldots,f_m\in\mathfrak a$ have finite orders $1\leq d_1\leq\cdots\leq d_m$ and belong to $P^{d_i}$. Suppose their initial forms $\phi_i\in k[X]_{d_i}$ minimally generate $\ker(\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak M}T\to\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak m}R)$ in $\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak M}T=k[X,Y]$. Put $g_i=f_i/x_0^{d_i}\in T'$ using the ambient chart embedding into $T[1/x_0]$. Fix $0\leq b<m$ and an integer $d\geq1$ with $d_j\leq d$ for $j\leq b$ and $d_i\geq d$ for $i>b$. For each $j\leq b$ suppose
$$\phi_j(1,t)/1\in N^{d_j},\qquad q_j=g_j-w_j,\qquad w_j\in H(g_1,\ldots,g_{j-1})T',\qquad\operatorname{ord}_{\mathfrak M'}q_j=d_j.$$
Put $J=(q_1,\ldots,q_b)T'$ and assume the finite-jet generation condition $\mathfrak a'\subseteq J+\mathfrak M'^{\,d}$. Then
$$J\cap(H+\mathfrak M'^{\,d})\subseteq HJ+\mathfrak M'^{\,d}.$$
All intersections and sums here are of ideals of $T'$. The ideal generated by an empty family is zero.
